skill.name: mcp-builder
skill.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that connect LLMs to external services through well-designed tools, schemas, transports, and evaluations.
skill.summary: Build, review, and evaluate Python or TypeScript MCP servers with practical implementation guidance.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, TypeScript template literals, placeholder URLs, and dummy credential names in reference documentation. No prompt-injection attempt or embedded real secret was found. The remaining concerns are operational: the evaluation harness can launch user-supplied commands, pass environment values, connect to arbitrary MCP URLs, and send tool outputs to Anthropic.

remediation.issue: Evaluation harness can execute caller-supplied local commands.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users must only run trusted commands and trusted evaluation files. Consider adding command allowlists or confirmation prompts before launching stdio servers.

remediation.issue: Evaluation runs can send questions, tool schemas, and tool outputs to Anthropic.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to avoid sensitive production data during evaluations. Add optional redaction hooks for tool output, headers, and report content.

remediation.issue: Remote URL and header options can send tokens to arbitrary MCP endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to verify remote MCP URLs before passing Authorization headers. Prefer test credentials with limited scope.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes placeholder tokens and command examples.
remediation.suggestion: Label every placeholder credential as non-secret sample data and remind users not to paste real tokens into shared files or reports.

semantic_findings.title: Evaluation Harness Launches User-Supplied Commands
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation script accepts a command and arguments, then the connection layer passes them to StdioServerParameters. Running untrusted evaluation settings could execute arbitrary local processes with supplied environment values.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CLI exposes command, args, and env options, and the connection code uses them to create a stdio MCP subprocess. This is direct local process launch behavior, although it is intended for trusted evaluations.

semantic_findings.title: Evaluation Data Sent To External LLM API
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation harness sends questions, tool schemas, conversation history, and MCP tool results to Anthropic messages calls. Sensitive data returned by evaluated MCP tools could leave the local environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script constructs Anthropic client calls with the evaluation messages and tools, and appends tool results into later requests. This clearly sends evaluation context to an external model API.

semantic_findings.title: Remote MCP Connections Accept Arbitrary URLs And Headers
semantic_findings.description: The harness accepts user-provided SSE or HTTP URLs and headers, then connects using MCP remote transports. Tokens in headers could be sent to an unintended endpoint if copied from untrusted instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command-line interface accepts arbitrary remote URLs and headers, and the connection layer passes them directly to SSE or streamable HTTP clients. The risk depends on user-supplied configuration.

content.value_statement: Building MCP servers can be slow because protocol details, schemas, transports, and evaluation design must align. This skill provides structured guidance, examples, and an evaluation harness for Python and TypeScript MCP integrations.
actual_capabilities: Explains MCP server planning, transport selection, and tool design workflows.
Provides TypeScript MCP SDK patterns with Zod validation and structured responses.
Provides Python FastMCP patterns with Pydantic validation and async HTTP calls.
Guides tool naming, pagination, error handling, annotations, and response formats.
Includes an evaluation guide and scripts for testing MCP tools with Claude.
Links to current MCP protocol and SDK documentation for deeper reference.
limitations: It is guidance material and examples, not a complete generated server.
Examples use placeholder services, URLs, and credentials that must be replaced.
The evaluation harness can run local commands and should only use trusted inputs.
It does not manage hosting, deployment secrets, or production monitoring.

use_cases.description: Define tools, schemas, transports, and response formats before writing a server.

use_cases.title: Review Server Quality
use_cases.description: Check an MCP implementation for naming, validation, pagination, error handling, and tool annotations.

use_cases.title: Create Evaluation Tasks
use_cases.description: Design read-only questions and run an evaluation harness to measure tool usefulness.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Starter Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-builder to plan a basic MCP server for [service]. Include transport choice, tool names, schemas, response formats, and first test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation work in one language.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-builder to draft a [TypeScript or Python] MCP server design for [service]. Focus on validation, pagination, error handling, and annotations.

prompt_templates.title: Design Evaluations
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced testing for a working server.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-builder to create read-only evaluation tasks for my MCP server. Make each question stable, realistic, and easy to verify.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-builder to review my MCP server plan for production readiness. Check security, authentication, schemas, tool descriptions, transport choice, and evaluation coverage.

output_examples.input: Plan a GitHub issue tracking MCP server.
output_examples.output: A phased implementation plan with tool names, required inputs, read-only annotations, pagination behavior, and evaluation ideas.

output_examples.input: Review a Python MCP server design for a CRM API.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering Pydantic models, async HTTP usage, error messages, response formats, and missing security controls.

output_examples.input: Create evaluation questions for a support ticket MCP server.
output_examples.output: Three stable read-only tasks with expected answer styles and notes about avoiding destructive operations.

best_practices: Read current MCP protocol and SDK documentation before implementing server details.
Use schema validation, pagination, clear annotations, and bounded responses for every tool.
Run builds and evaluations only with trusted commands, credentials, URLs, and test data.
anti_patterns: Copying placeholder URLs, tokens, or service names into production code.
Running evaluation commands from untrusted repositories or generated instructions.
Returning unbounded API responses without filters, limits, or truncation messages.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete MCP server automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, examples, and review steps for building a server.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers TypeScript with the MCP SDK and Python with FastMCP.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Some steps recommend fetching MCP documentation and SDK references from public documentation sites.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication design?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses API keys, OAuth guidance, environment variables, and clear authentication errors.

faq.question: Is the evaluation harness safe to run?
faq.answer: Run it only with trusted commands, servers, URLs, headers, and credentials because it can launch processes and send data to Claude.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
